_comment: Authoritative ground-truth set of planted vulnerabilities in demo_project/.
Line numbers were located by reading demo_project/*.py directly (not inferred).
Fields: id, file (relative to demo_project/), category, line_start, line_end (inclusive), description.
The eval matcher (benchmark/eval.py) matches a finding to an entry when:
basename(file) matches AND normalized category matches AND the reported line is
within +/- fuzz lines (default 5) of [line_start, line_end]; matching is one-to-one.
Entries with "provisional": true are NOT counted toward the scored ground truth
unless eval.py is run with --include-provisional. See README 'Benchmark' subsection.
Category strings are the authoritative human labels; eval.py normalizes them
(e.g. 'Weak Crypto' <-> the tool's 'Secrets Exposure') before comparing.
An entry may set "accepted_categories" (defaults to [category]) to list more
than one valid category when the planted vulnerability genuinely spans them
(e.g. an unauthenticated arbitrary-SQL endpoint is both SQLi and Auth Bypass).
This only relaxes the category check; the file and +/- line gates are unchanged.

vulnerabilities.description: build_search_query: string-interpolated LIKE clause (search_term/role_filter injected into SQL).
build_update_query: SET values and user_id interpolated without parameterization.
build_export_query: user-controlled sort_field injected directly into ORDER BY.
execute_query / execute_read: raw SQL string sinks passed to conn.execute with no parameter binding.
require_auth: accepts any token present in VALID_TOKENS without checking expiry or scope.
check_permission: logic bug falls through to 'return True', granting access to non-admins.
hash_password: MD5 used for password hashing (the hashlib.md5 call is on line 34).

/api/admin/run-query (run_raw_query): executes arbitrary client-supplied SQL with no auth check. This endpoint is genuinely both SQLi (raw client SQL reaches execute_read) and an Auth Bypass (no auth on a privileged route); the scanner correctly characterizes it either way, so both categories are accepted for this single planted vulnerability.
delete_user: f-string SQL injection on user_id into a DELETE statement.
impersonate_user: f-string SQL injection on user_id into an INSERT (also no expiry/audit).
update_user_profile: calls check_permission but ignores its return value, so access is never enforced.
export_users: forwards unvalidated sort_field to build_export_query -> execute_read (SQLi sink).

vulnerabilities.provisional_reason: RECONSTRUCTED/ADDED for review confirmation. search_users forwards the unvalidated 'query' parameter into build_search_query -> execute_read (a SQLi sink). This is a genuine vulnerability present in user_service.py beyond the two labeled entries, and Autopsy repeatedly flagged it in historical runs (user_service.py:10-11). NOT counted in the scored ground truth unless eval.py is run with --include-provisional. Pending author confirmation.
